description.narrative: Australia is a long-standing strategic partner of the Indonesian education system. In support of the Merdeka Belajar (meaning ‘Emancipated Learning’) reforms, Australia’s Innovation for Indonesia's Schools Children (INOVASI) program enables the development and trial of a range of transformative reforms. To support inclusive student-centred learning approaches these include a more flexible curriculum, improvements to teacher training, and increased use of learner-focused technologies in classrooms. ‍ In planning a new phase of the partnership, the Government of Indonesia leveraged its membership of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) to extend the reach and impact of the successful INOVASI model. Australia and Indonesia accessed US$24.2 million in GPE Multiplier funds, complementing Australia’s new investments in the sector. Through the GPE Multiplier, Save the Children will scale up the INOVASI program to support student learning, climate change adaptation and child protection in North Sumatra, Lampung, West Kalimantan and North Maluku provinces.

Since 2021, US$575.5 million (A$882.8 million) in new Indo-Pacific Global Partnership for Education (GPE) grants have been approved. With the addition of legacy grants, Australia is strategically engaged with Indo-Pacific countries and GPE partners for the effective roll-out of a US$1.02 billion (A$1.56 billion) Indo-Pacific portfolio. In consultation with DFAT and Pacific Island Countries, a GPE Pacific regional partnership package is in development. Through its position on the GPE Board, Australia is engaging on priorities for the next GPE Strategic Plan (GPE 2030), including an ongoing focus on Small Island Developing States and Southeast Asia’s developing economies. In alignment with Australia’s International Development Policy, GPE will continue to ‘hard-wire’ gender equality, prioritise disability equity and rights, and scale-up climate change and education linkages.

Through Australia’s Global Partnership for Education (GPE) investment, improvements in student learning is a core priority. This is reflected in the ‘GPE 2025’ – its strategic plan – and is put into practice through the US$807 million in active GPE grants in the Indo-Pacific. ‍
‍ A core component of GPE 2025 is the ‘Partnership Compact’. Led by national governments, Partnership Compacts are technically reviewed and endorsed by Australia and other development actors. The eighteen completed Compacts across the Indo-Pacific seek to transform education systems by asking the question: What one reform will make the greatest difference in improving education access, participation and learning? Across the Indo-Pacific, the answer given by partner governments is continuing to build inclusive, high quality education systems. Better student learning is fundamental to prosperity and stability in our diverse and ever-changing region. Australia’s investments through GPE and other partners is bringing practical support to learning for all.
